source: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 16 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 16
knowledgePattern: Negate a compound sufficient condition using the contrapositive
solution:
Let P mean A is right, Q mean B is left, and R mean C is right. The supplied implication is: P AND (Q OR R) implies the safe is open.

Its contrapositive says: if the safe is closed, then NOT [P AND (Q OR R)]. Negating the whole expression gives (NOT P) OR [(NOT Q) AND (NOT R)].

Each lever has only left and right positions. Therefore, if the safe is closed, A is left, or both B is right and C is left. This is option D. The original rule does not say the stated opening condition is the only way to open the safe.

hints.title: Reverse the implication correctly
hints.body: Use the contrapositive to obtain a guaranteed statement when the safe is closed. Keep the whole lever condition inside brackets while negating it.
hints.recap: A statement and its contrapositive are equivalent; its converse need not follow.
hints.pitfall: The opening condition is sufficient; it has not been stated to be necessary.
hints.pause: Write the negation of the complete lever condition.

recall.reminder: A statement and its contrapositive are equivalent; its converse need not follow.

hints.title: Negate one pair of brackets at a time
hints.body: Apply the AND/OR negation rules from the outer brackets inward, then translate each negated lever position.
hints.recap: Negating AND produces an OR of negations; negating OR produces an AND of negations.
hints.pitfall: Preserve the grouping; changing one AND or OR can change the guarantee.
hints.pause: Simplify your logical expression and match its grouping to an option.

recall.reminder: Negating AND produces an OR of negations; negating OR produces an AND of negations.
